title: Add Support Escalation workflow (modal + required fields + playbook links + optional Jira key)
author: Miles Thornton
description: Adds a first-class “Support Escalation” workflow to incident-bot to standardize intake when Support/CS needs Engineering/SRE engagement. This is intentionally lighter-weight than full incident declaration but captures the same core metadata so oncall can triage quickly and we can keep comms consistent. The workflow is launched via /incident-bot support-escalation (alias: /ib support-escalation) and presents a Slack modal with required fields aligned to Escalation Playbook v2. On submit, the bot creates (or reuses) a dedicated thread in #incidents (configurable) with a structured summary block, pins the summary, and posts follow-up prompts (comms cadence + next steps). Required-field enforcement blocks submission when critical metadata is missing (deployment mode, customer tier, impact, timeframe, region, request IDs or an explicit “no request IDs available” checkbox). Also includes optional Jira key capture (SUP-/INT-) and optional Linear key capture, which are rendered as links in the posted summary. Links are included to the Confluence playbook landing page and the “required fields” checklist so the thread can be used as the single source of truth during escalation. Notes: (1) no customer-identifying data is persisted by the bot beyond what’s in the Slack messages; (2) we added guardrails for “restricted account” escalations to avoid pasting sensitive identifiers—modal copy nudges teams to use internal IDs and attach logs via approved channels. Rollout: behind a feature flag SUPPORT_ESCALATION_WORKFLOW_ENABLED defaulting to true in staging and false in prod until Support training completes; prod enable is a config-only change.
commits: feat(workflows): add Support Escalation workflow entrypoint + routing
feat(slack): implement support escalation modal + validation rules
feat(posting): structured thread summary + pin + follow-up prompts
feat(linking): render optional Jira/Linear keys as links; add Confluence playbook links
chore(config): add feature flag + env wiring + defaults
test: add workflow validation and payload snapshot tests
docs: update README with /ib support-escalation usage
checks: CI (ubuntu-latest): lint ✅ | typecheck ✅ | unit-tests ✅ | build ✅ | slack-manifest-validate ✅. Initial run failed on slack-manifest-validate due to missing command alias registration; fixed in 8f2c1d9 and reran successfully.
conversation:
Miles Thornton (author): “Context: part of Escalation Playbook v2 rollout. Support asked for a consistent intake path that doesn’t always require declaring an incident, but still collects request IDs / region / model / timeframe. This implements the workflow in incident-bot so the ‘escalation thread’ has a predictable format.”

Rafael Mendes (review): “Love the direction. Two asks: (1) make request IDs required OR an explicit checkbox that they’re unavailable; we keep getting escalations with zero traces. (2) Default channel should remain #incidents for now to match oncall monitoring. Also, can you add a ‘current mitigation/workaround applied?’ field?”

Miles Thornton (author): “Done. Added requestIdUnavailable boolean and validation. Added mitigation/workaround multi-line input (required for Sev0/Sev1, optional otherwise). Channel is now configurable but defaults to #incidents.”

Owen Phillips (review): “Modal copy: can we align terminology to the playbook? Use ‘Severity (P0–P4)’ and ‘Customer tier (Self-serve/Dedicated/Private/Enterprise)’. Also please add a link to the Confluence required-fields checklist in the posted thread.”

Miles Thornton (author): “Updated labels and options to match playbook language. Thread header now includes: Escalation Playbook v2 + Required Fields links.”

Priya Shah (review): “Known-issues sprint angle: can we add a quick select for ‘issue category’ (429s / streaming disconnects / timeouts / 5xx / auth/SSO / dedicated capacity) so Support can tag quickly? Even if it’s not used for automation yet, it helps triage.”

Miles Thornton (author): “Added ‘Category’ dropdown. Stored only in message payload; no backend persistence. We can later map this to routing hints.”

Tomáš Novák (review): “Paging hygiene: please ensure this workflow does NOT page oncall by itself. It should post to #incidents and rely on humans for paging. Also add a line in the follow-up prompt reminding folks: ‘escalation != incident’ and link to incident declaration criteria.”

Miles Thornton (author): “Confirmed no paging hooks in this workflow. Added follow-up message with ‘When to declare an incident’ link (Confluence oncall process) + reminder on criteria.”

Allison Grant (review): “Observability ask: include a standardized block for metrics/dashboards: ‘check streaming_disconnect_rate, timeout_rate’ with placeholder links. Even if empty, it nudges best practice.”

Miles Thornton (author): “Added an optional ‘Dashboards/metrics checked’ field and a templated hint block in the thread (no hardcoded Grafana URLs; we kept it generic + runbook links).”

Rafael Mendes (final): “Ship it. This will materially improve time-to-triage.”

Merged by Miles Thornton via squash merge.
release_notes:
- New /ib support-escalation command (alias: /incident-bot support-escalation) opens a standardized Support Escalation modal.
- Enforces required metadata (tier, deployment mode, impact, timeframe, region, request IDs or explicit ‘unavailable’).
- Posts structured escalation summary in #incidents thread with Confluence playbook + required-fields links.
- Optional Jira (SUP-/INT-) and Linear key capture rendered as links.
- Feature-flagged rollout via SUPPORT_ESCALATION_WORKFLOW_ENABLED.
